intro: Searching for a sedation dentist near you usually means you're anxious about dental treatment, or you need a procedure that's hard to face without some help. You want to find a local practice where conscious sedation is available, and you'd like to understand what that involves before you book. iComply introduces you to a private dentist who can quote you directly for sedation dentistry.
need_heading: What people searching for a sedation dentist usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a sedation dentist near them have a specific worry or treatment in mind and want to know how sedation could help.
needs: You feel very anxious about dental visits and have put off treatment for a long time.
You need a filling, extraction or other procedure that feels too daunting to have without sedation.
You have a strong gag reflex that makes routine treatment difficult.
You want to find a practice close to home that offers conscious sedation, such as IV or inhalation sedation.
You need to understand how sedation works, including that you'll need an escort home afterwards.
context_heading: What to understand about sedation dentistry
context: Conscious sedation is not a general anaesthetic. It helps you feel relaxed and less anxious during treatment, but you stay conscious and can respond to your dentist. Your medical history will be checked carefully beforehand to make sure sedation is safe for you.

After IV sedation you will need someone to escort you home and stay with you for a while. It's important to arrange this in advance, as you won't be able to drive or travel home alone. Sedation dentists are registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales the regulator is Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your level of dental anxiety and any past experiences that have made you nervous.
Explain what treatment you think you need, or what your dentist has told you.
Mention any medical conditions or medications you take, as these affect sedation options.
Say whether you have a preference for IV sedation or inhalation sedation, if you know.
Confirm you can arrange an escort home after IV sedation.
Give your location and how far you're willing to travel to find a suitable dentist.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the sedation dentist
questions: What type of sedation do you offer, and which would you recommend for my treatment?
How will you check my medical history and make sure sedation is safe for me?
Will I need someone to escort me home, and how long should they stay with me?
Can you explain what conscious sedation will feel like and how I might feel afterwards?
What is your experience of treating anxious patients with sedation?
What happens if I need further treatment after sedation – how is that arranged?

faqs.a: Conscious sedation is generally safe when carried out by a trained dentist after a careful check of your medical history. Your dentist will discuss any risks with you beforehand and make sure you understand what to expect.

faqs.q: Will I be asleep during sedation?
faqs.a: No, conscious sedation is not a general anaesthetic. You will be relaxed and may feel drowsy, but you remain conscious and able to respond to your dentist.

faqs.q: Can I drive home after IV sedation?
faqs.a: No, you must not drive after IV sedation. You will need someone to escort you home and stay with you for a period afterwards, so it's important to arrange this in advance.

faqs.q: How do I know the dentist is qualified?
faqs.a: All dentists must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must also register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings; in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland different regulators apply.
